notes: Ran it, did not read it. by_severity: present iff a non-PASS row exists (absent on an all-PASS round), identical on the --json and -o forms, survives --compact while overlap_report drops, four named buckets with no "" key, sums to findings, and error+unrecognised=5 equals the blocking population over a fixture holding all four unrecognised shapes. 20 runs hash-identical (Go sorts map keys). inputs/rows are [], by_status/by_role {} when empty. Exits 2/3 verified.

Pins the §4 contract at the level the role rules ask for: presence keyed on rows not cleanliness (advisory-only fixture under both policies), the -o form as well as stdout, absence on an all-PASS round, --compact with overlap_report as the control arm, no "" bucket, exactly four bucket names, buckets summing to findings, and the population being the deduplicated rows. Expectations derive through engine.AuditRowsClean rather than restating literals. Green on -count=1.

budget_exhausted is OMITTED when audit_max_rounds is 0 (the built-in default), while its siblings max_rounds and rounds_remaining are emitted as explicit null. Measured: uncapped `tp audit spec.md --status` carries no budget_exhausted key; after `tp set --workflow audit_max_rounds=3` it appears as false. SKILL.md:146 lists it among what --status shows, qualifying only max_rounds/rounds_remaining as null when uncapped. Same on review (SKILL.md:76). Pre-existing, outside v0.37.0's surface.

Both §2 branches on both sinks, asserted as textual difference against an empty round rather than presence, plus the converged arm still naming no tp command. Verified by running: "2 accepted rows carried forward - run the next audit round" and "converged over 1 accepted row", both surviving --compact. One weak assertion: assert.Contains(withRows, "3") is a bare substring passing on any payload holding a 3; the noun phrase is pinned only at engine level (nextaction_test.go:162-163).

Both stamping directions, asserted on state.json bytes AND on the audit_rounds[] the --status payload carries AND on the derived signals, so a report-side re-grade that leaves the store honest is still caught. Confirmed by running: audit_rounds[] entries carry round/findings/clean/recorded_at/file/spec_hash/roles_hash/id_scheme, so an agent reads the per-round verdict beside the raw count and can tell a blocking-stamped round (clean true beside findings > 0) without a vintage byte.

deviations and skipped are both make(...,0) so they serialize as [] and never null; skipped is added only when non-empty, matching the omitted-not-null convention divergence uses. Ran it: a task-level blocking under a project-level all reports one deviation with keys field/file/override/project sorted, exit 0, exit 1 under --strict. An illegal literal is reported as the deviation it is rather than graded - confirmed by storing "nope" and seeing exit 0 here while both audit sinks exit 1.

TestWorkflowDeviations_AuditConvergeOn covers the field on the same terms as its review twin: differing values report, equal values do not, and a project layer that does not set the field carries no policy so nothing deviates. Nothing else here is in this role's domain; the emitted shape it asserts matches what the binary printed when run.

The payload-shape guards this role cares about are all present and green: role_streaks an emitted array and spec_coverage_clean_rounds an emitted null on empty state, divergence an omitted key rather than JSON null, all three surviving --compact whole, absent from every other output, and a streak entry pinned at exactly three keys (line 560) so no scope label or per-role threshold arrives unnoticed. Confirmed by running: empty state prints audit_rounds [], role_streaks [], overlap_report [].

The change is the rename countAuditFindings -> parseAuditRows plus its second return value; both assertions are unchanged and green. Rejection is still one round-trip: every offending line is named at once and the message enumerates the enum. Measured a cost outside this file: `tp audit --merge` accepts a category outside the enum silently (exit 0, no stderr warning) and `tp audit --record` then rejects the merged file with exit 1, so a bad category costs two commands.

Well-formed manifest, keys unchanged, keywords a non-empty array. Nothing in the agent-facing command-output contract lives here. Two maintainer notes rather than defects of this release: version reads 0.36.1 while the cycle under audit is v0.37.0, and CLAUDE.md's pre-release step 4b makes the bump mandatory before tagging (hooks/session-start.sh reads the same field as the minimum tp version); and the author name was re-encoded to \u00f6 escapes this cycle.
